HistoryDescription:
Gunbalunya is a mostly Aboriginal community, east of Jabiru in western Arnhem Land and 320km east of Darwin.

Originally established by Paddy Cahill as his homestead in 1906 when he took up a Pastoral Lease in the area and established a diary herd there.   Cahill named his property Oenpelli, an anglisised pronounciation of the name Un-balange.

In 1916 Gilruth's administration acquired Cahill herd and employed his as manager. In October 1925 the Church Mission Society took up a 2000 sq km lease in the area and managed the community until the 1970s when the Gunbalanya Council Inc.  was registered and took over management of the community following the Government's policy of self-determination.

The Kunbarllanjnja Community Government Council was established in 1995.

In 2001, following a request from the Council the name Oenpelli was changed to Gunbalanya, a name the council considered easier to pronounce than the more traditional Kunbarllanjnja.

Name: GUNYANGARA
Description: The community of Ski Beach is located on Gunyangara Island in Melville Bay.  The small island is joined to the mainland by a causeway at Drimmie Peninsula west of Nhulunbuy.  Ski Beach is 13 km west of Nhulunbuy CBD.  From Nhulunbuy CBD the community is accessible via Melville Bay Road, 8 km of sealed road then 5 km of dirt road, travel time is 10 mins.

Services.Comments: By road, the community is 13 km west of Nhulunbuy township. From Nhulunbuy CBD the community is accessible via Melville Bay Road, 8 km of sealed road, approximate travel time 10 mins.
Check Road Report NT and Check the tides before travelling
Gove Peninsula Public Bus (NEAL) runs Monday to Friday between Yirrkala - Gunyangara - Gumatj Retail Precinct, and costs $10/person. Phone 8987 0900 for enquiries.
Available at BP in Nhulunbuy (13 km east of Gunyangara) and Rirrajtingu Fuel at Yirrkala (29km southeast).

Accommodation is available by commercial providers at Wallaby Beach Accommodation (also known as the Rirratjingu Workers Camp) 4km north Gunyangara. In Nhulunbuy, 14km to the east (a 15min drive), providers include Yanawal Units, Walkabout Lodge and Campsite, Manyimi Campground, and BanuBanu Lodge.
Gopu Community Store (8987 1306) sells groceries, fresh produce, hot lunches, coffee, and have an adjacent nursery. The store is open Monday to Friday 7am - 3pm and is managed by Gumatj corporation.

Projects.Title: AIR IN EAST ARNHEM: CROWDSOURCING AIR QUALITY, TEMPERATURE, AND HEALTH DATA WITH YOLNGU CITIZEN SCIENTISTS
Projects.Description: EXTREME HEAT AND AIR POLLUTION BOTH RESULT IN SEVERE NEGATIVE CONSEQUENCES ON HEALTH. INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES ARE PARTICULARLY AT RISK TO THESE ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS DUE TO THE HIGH BURDEN OF DISEASE. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO MONITOR AIR QUALITY AND TEMPERATURE DATA WITH THE HELP OF YOLNGU CITIZEN SCIENTISTS AND CO-DESIGN A SUSTAINABLE ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH RESPONSE IN THREE EAST ARNHEM REMOTE COMMUNITIES.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Gunyangara is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply. Electricity supply for Gunyangara is purchased from Rio Tinto.
Gunyangara has a plentiful groundwater source with very good quality water, which is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Gunyangara has a fully reticulated sewerage system.
Yolgnu Matha(Gumatj)
East Arnhem Regional Council
Nhulunbuy
Gunyangara is located on Gunyangara Island in Melville Bay. The small island is joined to the mainland by a causeway at Drimmie Peninsula west of Nhulunbuy.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Haasts Bluff is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Haasts Bluff has a plentiful groundwater source with marginal quality water, which is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Houses and buildings at Haasts Bluff are fitted with private septic systems.
Luritja/Pintupi
MacDonnell Regional Council
Namatjira

Haasts Bluff is located west of Alice Springs on the Haasts Bluff Aboriginal Land Trust  amongst the West MacDonnell Ranges. To the north is Ulampawarru and Anyali (Mt Edward and Mt William), and to the south is the stunning Mereenie Bluff.

Name: HERMANNSBURG
Description:
The community is located 130km west of Alice Springs by road and it takes 1.5 hours to drive there. By air, it takes 5 minutes to drive to the closest airstrip in the community, and then 35 minutes to fly to Alice Springs.

The 130 km access road to the community from Alice Springs is along Larapinta Drive, and is sealed the entire distance. The 2 km from Larapinta Drive to the community is unsealed gravel. The same road bypasses the community to give access to Areyonga, the Mereenie oil and gas fields, Palm Valley and Kings Canyon.

Services.Comments: The 130 km access road to the community from Alice Springs is along Larapinta Drive, and is sealed the entire distance. It's around 1.5 hrs drives from Alice Springs, however can be cut off due to heavy rain for short periods.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Hermannsburg is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply. Hermannsburg is connected to the Alice Springs electricity grid.
Hermannsburg has a limited groundwater source with adequate quality water, which is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Hermannsburg has a fully reticulated sewerage system.
Western Arrernte
MacDonnell Regional Council
Namatjira
Hermannsburg is located west of Alice Springs on the Ntaria Aboriginal Land Trust just north of the Finke George National Park and on the banks of the Finke River

Name: IMANPA
Description: The community is located in the Northern Territory of Australia. It is located 7 km north of the Lasseters Highway, the main road running between the Stuart Highway and Uluru (Ayers Rock). Imanpa lies 160 km east of Uluru and 200 km south west of Alice Springs. It is seventeen kilometres from Mt Ebenezer Roadhouse, which is also owned and run by the community, along with Angus Downs Station.

Services.Comments: The community is accessible by road (Lasseters Highway) from Alice Springs. The Lasseters Highway is sealed to the community turn off.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Imanpa is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Imanpa has a limited groundwater source with marginal quality water. The water supply has aeration treatment, is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Imanpa has a fully reticulated sewerage system.

PopulationIndicators.Label: Median age of persons
PopulationIndicators.Comments: Median age (in years) of the population at the time of the Census (excludes overseas visitors).

PopulationIndicators.Label: Median total personal income ($/weekly)
PopulationIndicators.Comments: Median total personal income ($/ weekly) at the time of the Census. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and over.

PopulationIndicators.Label: Median total family income ($/weekly)
PopulationIndicators.Comments: Median total family income ($/ weekly) at the time of the Census.

PopulationIndicators.Label: Median total household income ($/weekly)
PopulationIndicators.Comments: Median total household income ($/weekly) at the time of the Census. It excludes 'Visitors only' and 'Other non-classifiable' households.

PopulationIndicators.Label: Average number of persons per bedroom
PopulationIndicators.Comments: Average number of persons per bedroom at the time of the Census. It excludes 'Visitors only' and 'Other non-classifiable' households.

PopulationIndicators.Label: Average household size
PopulationIndicators.Comments: Average number of persons per household at the time of the Census. It excludes 'Visitors only' and 'Other non-classifiable' households.

PopulationIndicators.Label: Percent households where rent payments are more than 30% of household (RAID) income
PopulationIndicators.Comments: Proportion of households for whom rent payments were more than 30% of household income at the time of the Census.

LabourForceIndicators.Label: % Unemployment
LabourForceIndicators.Comments: Unemployment rate (%) at the time of the Census. This is the number of unemployed persons expressed as a percentage of the total labour force. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and older.

LabourForceIndicators.Label: % Labour force participation
LabourForceIndicators.Comments: Labour force participation rate (%) at the time of the Census. This is the number of unemployed persons expressed as a percentage of the total labour force. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and older.

LabourForceIndicators.Label: % Employment to population
LabourForceIndicators.Comments: Employment to population rate (%) at the time of the Census. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and older.

HealthCareIndicators.Label: Rates of core activity need for assistance
HealthCareIndicators.Comments: Number of people with a profound or severe core activity limitation. People with a profound or severe core activity limitation are those needing assistance in their day to day lives.

HealthCareIndicators.Label: Rates of long-term health conditions (per 1,000)
HealthCareIndicators.Comments: Rates of long-term health conditions (per 1, 000 population). This measures the number of people who reported that they have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have any of these long-term health conditions.

HealthCareIndicators.Label: Rates of caring (unpaid) for a person with a disability, health condition, or due to old age
HealthCareIndicators.Comments: Rates of unpaid caring provided to a person with a disability, health condition, or due to old age (%).

Name: JABIRU
Description: The Town is located 250 km from Darwin by sealed road east of Darwin in Kakadu National Park.
HistoryDesc:
The mining town arose out of discoveries of Uranium at Kakadu in 1970 and the "Jabiru" airstrip to service the mining camp.  The Fox Royal Commission provided for the mining town to be established in connection with the Ranger Uranium deposit.

The name was derived from that bird that frequents the billabongs of the coastal plains of Kakadu.

Services.Comments: Bininj Kunwok Regional Language and Culture Centre

Access to Jabiru town is via two Highways. From Darwin via the Arnhem Highway heading East to Jabiru is approximately 254kms. From Pine Creek, south of Jabiru the Kakadu Highway is approximately 211kms. 2 wheel drive vehicle access is limited to both sealed highways that generally remain open throughout the year. During the Wet season (November to April) flooding associated with heavy rains may have various locational temporary closures. Check road report on: https://roadreport.nt.gov.au/road-map.

Projects.Title: THE BININJ DJENJ PROJECT: FISH, WATERWAYS AND ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE
Projects.Description: THE ALLIGATOR RIVERS REGION IN THE NORTHERN TERRITORY IS VULNERABLE TO ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE, WITH RISING SEA LEVELS A THREAT TO THE LOCAL WORLD HERITAGE LISTED FRESHWATER WETLANDS. THE BININJ DJENJ PROJECT WILL TRAIN CITIZEN SCIENTISTS TO WORK IN PARTNERSHIP WITH RESEARCHERS AND TEACHERS TO COLLECT DATA ON LOCAL FISH POPULATIONS AND WATER QUALITY, THUS ASSISTING IN MONITORING THE HEALTH OF THE LOCAL HYDROLOGICAL SYSTEMS. DATA ON MODERN FISH SPECIES WILL BE COMPARED WITH ANCIENT FISH REMAINS FROM THE 65,000YO MADJEDBEBE ARCHAEOLOGICAL SITE TO INVESTIGATE FISH RESPONSES TO PAST ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE AND TO SUPPORT FUTURE HUMAN AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESILIENCE IN THE REGION.

AliasNameDescription: The community Jabiru is not known to have any other aliases.
HistoryDescription:
The mining town arose out of discoveries of Uranium at Kakadu in 1970 and the "Jabiru" airstrip to service the mining camp.  The Fox Royal Commission provided for the mining town to be established in connection with the Ranger Uranium deposit.

The name was derived from that bird that frequents the billabongs of the coastal plains of Kakadu.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Jilkminggan is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply. Jilkminggan is connected to the Katherine electricity grid.
Jilkminggan has a plentiful groundwater source with marginal quality water, which is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Jilkminggan has a fully reticulated sewerage system.
Eastside Kriol
Roper Gulf Regional Council
Barkly
Jilkminggan is located south east of Katherine near Elsey National Park on the Mangarrayi Aboriginal Land Trust.

LabourForceIndicators.Comments: Unemployment rate (%) at the time of the Census. This is the number of unemployed persons expressed as a percentage of the total labour force. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and older.

LabourForceIndicators.Label: % Labour force participation
LabourForceIndicators.Comments: Labour force participation rate (%) at the time of the Census. This is the number of unemployed persons expressed as a percentage of the total labour force. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and older.

LabourForceIndicators.Label: % Employment to population
LabourForceIndicators.Comments: Employment to population rate (%) at the time of the Census. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and older.

HealthCareIndicators.Label: Rates of core activity need for assistance
HealthCareIndicators.Comments: Number of people with a profound or severe core activity limitation. People with a profound or severe core activity limitation are those needing assistance in their day to day lives.

Services.Comments: Access to Kalkarindji from Katherine is via the Victoria and Buntine highways. The road is sealed between the Victoria Highway turnoff and Kalkarindji, with the section between Kalkarindji and the Western Australia border unsealed. Depending on weather and road conditions, it is about a five to six hours drive.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Kalkarindji/Daguragu is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply. Daguragu is connected to the Kalkarindji electricity grid.

Kalkarindji and Daguragu share the same groundwater source which has limited capacity but good quality water. The two communities have separate water supplies which are chlorinated and monitored monthly for microbes.
Kalkarindji and Daguragu have separate fully reticulated sewerage systems.
Gurindji / Kriol
Victoria Daly Regional Council
Stuart
Kalkarindji is located south west of Katherine near the boarder of Wave Hill Pastoral Property and Daguragu community.

Name: KALTUKATJARA
Description:
The community is located 670km southwest from Alice Springs by road via Uluru and it takes 7 hours to drive.  By air it is 495 km and is a 1.5-hour flight to Alice Springs.

The road from Alice Springs to the community is both sealed & unsealed. The last 190 km is dirt. The community is situated in the Petermann Ranges in the far south western corner of the Northern Territory, 7 kilometres east of the Western Australian border. The settlement is a few hundred metres from the dry bed of the Docker Creek.

Docker River has marginal quality water due to elevated levels of lead and some hardness. Capacity of the groundwater supply is adequate.
Docker River has a fully reticulated sewerage system.

Name: KATHERINE
Description: The Town is located 270km SE of Darwin.
HistoryDesc:
The town of Katherine was named after the Katherine River which in turn was named after Catherine Chambers by John McDouall Stuart, when he crossed it some 30 miles east of the present town in 1862.  
The Overland Telegraph Line crossing the River became the main habitation of the early years as well as the Springvale down stream, managed by Alfred Giles for Dr WJ Browne.  This eventually became the link with the west.  
Emungalan of some 40 lots became a temporary town until 1926 when the railway bridge across the Katherine River was constructed and the town of Katherine was gazetted on 1 July 1926 (CG 26) with later extensions on 1 December 1927 and 1951.  
However, by way of proclamation made on 28 March 1967 this town ceased to exist and a new town of Katherine gazetted (CG 43 18/05/1967 - extract appearing in NTG 29 24/5/1967).  There have been various extensions since then  (1970 and 1978), and the town now encompasses over 3734 hectares.

Projects.Title: ENSURING PROVISION OF ESSENTIAL PRIMARY HEALTH CARE SERVICES
Projects.Description: THE COMMONWEALTH HEALTH WORKFORCE PROGRAM DELIVERS HEATH WORKFORCE OUTCOMES AND SUPPORT FOR RURAL OUTREACH HEALTH SERVICES. THE HEALTH WORKFORCE PROGRAM IS DELIVERED UNDER THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND AGED CARE&RSQUO;S OUTCOME 1.4 &NDASH; HEALTH WORKFORCE. THIS OUTCOME IS INTENDED TO IMPROVE IMPROVE THE QUALITY, DISTRIBUTION AND PLANNING OF THE AUSTRALIAN HEALTH WORKFORCE TO BETTER MEET THE NEEDS OF THE COMMUNITY AND DELIVER A SUSTAINABLE, WELL DISTRIBUTED HEALTH WORKFORCE. IN THE 2022-23 BUDGET, THE AUSTRALIAN GOVERNMENT ANNOUNCED A LANDMARK LONG-TERM ENGAGEMENT WITH THE ROYAL FLYING DOCTOR SERVICE (RFDS OF AUSTRALIA). THIS ANNOUNCEMENT COMPRISES OF THIS &LSQUO;ENSURING PROVISION OF ESSENTIAL PRIMARY HEALTH CARE SERVICES IN RURAL AND REMOTE AUSTRALIA&RSQUO; PROGRAM, A 10-YEAR STRATEGIC AGREEMENT AND UP TO APPROXIMATELY $1 BILLION OVER A PERIOD OF UP TO TEN YEARS TO PROVIDE ESSENTIAL PRIMARY HEALTH CARE SERVICES AND AEROMEDICAL EVACUATIONS FOR RURAL AND REMOTE PATIENTS IN AREAS OF MARKET FAILURE OR BEYOND WHERE NORMAL MEDICAL INFRASTRUCTURE WOULD OTHERWISE PROVIDE SERVICES. THIS INCLUDES REFORM OF THE COMMONWEALTH&RSQUO;S PARTNERSHIP WITH THE RFDS OF AUSTRALIA TO INCLUDE COLLABORATIVE ANNUAL SERVICE PLANNING, AND INCREASED FLEXIBILITY AND RESPONSIVENESS IN FUNDING ALLOCATION AND SERVICE LEVELS TO ENSURE HEALTH SERVICES ARE DELIVERED TO THOSE COMMUNITIES MOST IN NEED, IN RURAL AND REMOTE AUSTRALIA.&NBSP;&NBSP;

PARTICIPANTS WILL TOUR AROUND MANGO AND AVOCADO ORCHARDS, COTTON, AND SPICE FIELD TRIALS, LEARN ABOUT TRACTORS, LIVESTOCK, WORKING DOGS, AND VISIT THE ENTOMOLOGY LAB TO FILL OUT WORKBOOKS FOR PRIZES. THE TOURS WILL BE FOLLOWED BY SHORT PRESENTATIONS FROM LOCAL SCIENTISTS AND FARMERS, AND STALLS FEATURING INTERACTIVE DISPLAYS SHOWING PLANT, INSECT, ANIMAL AND SOIL SCIENCE THEMES.

Projects.Title: PACIFICAUS SPORTS GRANTS SUPPORT PARTNERSHIPS IN RUGBY UNION, RUGBY LEAGUE, SOCCER, NETBALL, CRICKET, AFL AND PREPARATIONS FOR THE 2024 PARIS OLYMPICS AND PARALYMPICS, PRIMARILY IN FIJI, NAURU, PAPUA NEW GUINEA, SAMOA, SOLOMON ISLANDS, TONGA AND VANUATU.
Projects.Description: PACIFICAUS SPORTS&RSQUO; PURPOSE IS TO STRENGTHEN PEOPLE-TO-PEOPLE LINKS BETWEEN AUSTRALIA AND THE PACIFIC THROUGH SPORT TO ENHANCE AUSTRALIA&RSQUO;S RELATIONSHIPS AND STANDING IN THE PACIFIC. PACIFICAUS SPORTS DOES THIS BY FOSTERING ELITE SPORT PATHWAYS AND LINKAGES THAT FACILITATE REGULAR COMPETITION AND ENGAGEMENT BETWEEN AUSTRALIA AND PACIFIC TEAMS, ATHLETES AND OTHER SPORT STAKEHOLDERS. THE OBJECTIVES OF PACIFICAUS SPORTS PARTNERSHIP GRANTS ARE: (1) DEVELOPING PATHWAYS FOR PACIFIC TEAMS AND ATHLETES TO PLAY IN HIGH LEVEL AUSTRALIAN SPORTS COMPETITIONS: (2) SUPPORTING AUSTRALIAN SPORTS CODES TO INCREASE THEIR PRESENCE AND PARTICIPATION IN THE PACIFIC; AND (3) DEVELOPING PATHWAYS FOR EMERGING ATHLETES FROM THE REGION TO BENEFIT FROM HIGH PERFORMANCE COACHING, TRAINING, AND COMPETITION. THIS GRANT WILL ENABLE NETBALL AUSTRALIA TO CONTRIBUTE TO THESE OBJECTIVES USING NETBALL THROUGH ACTIVITIES INCLUDING SUPPORT FOR PACIFIC TEAMS AND PLAYERS TO COMPETE AND TRAIN IN AUSTRALIA, SUPPORT FOR AUSTRALIAN NETBALL CLUBS TO ENGAGE WITH THE PACIFIC, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF HIGH PERFORMANCE WORKSHOPS AND COACHING DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS.

HistoryDescription:
The town of Katherine was named after the Katherine River which in turn was named after Catherine Chambers by John McDouall Stuart, when he crossed it some 30 miles east of the present town in 1862.  
The Overland Telegraph Line crossing the River became the main habitation of the early years as well as the Springvale down stream, managed by Alfred Giles for Dr WJ Browne.  This eventually became the link with the west.  
Emungalan of some 40 lots became a temporary town until 1926 when the railway bridge across the Katherine River was constructed and the town of Katherine was gazetted on 1 July 1926 (CG 26) with later extensions on 1 December 1927 and 1951.  
However, by way of proclamation made on 28 March 1967 this town ceased to exist and a new town of Katherine gazetted (CG 43 18/05/1967 - extract appearing in NTG 29 24/5/1967).  There have been various extensions since then  (1970 and 1978), and the town now encompasses over 3734 hectares.

Name: KINTORE
Description:
The community is situated 530 kilometres west of Alice Springs. It is nestled at the base of culturally important hills known as Pulikatjara ('two hills'). The community is very remote. It is about six hours west of Alice Springs, in the middle of the western desert and is almost on the Western Australian border.

Road travel for the first 136km is via a bitumen all-weather road. The remainder of the journey is via dirt roads of varying quality. To access Pintubi travel north from Alice Springs and turn off at the Yuendumu turn off. Turn at the Papunya turn-off to a gravel road, which is in a very poor state (most of the year) and after approximately 105 km turn off towards Kintore. From there, the Papunya to Mt. Liebig turn off is approximately 66 km and then the Mt Liebig to Kintore turn-off is approximately 223 km. Although the total distance is about 530 km it takes approximately 6-7 hours to drive depending on the state of the road.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Kintore is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.

Kintore has a limited groundwater source with marginal quality water, which is disinfected with ultraviolet and monitored monthly for microbes. The water supply has an advanced water treatment plant which removes from drinking water identified naturally occurring minerals that exceed the recommended levels of the Australian Drinking Water Guidelines.
Kintore has a fully reticulated sewerage system.
Luritja/Pintupi
MacDonnell Regional Council
Namatjira

Kintore is located west of Alice Springs. It is nestled at the base of culturally important hills known as Pulikatjara ('two hills') near the Western Australia Border and part of the Haasts Bluff Aboriginal Land Trust.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Kybrook Farm is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply. Kybrook Farm is connected to the Katherine electricity grid.
Kybrook Farm has a limited groundwater source with marginal quality water, which is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Kybrook Farm has a fully reticulated sewerage system.
Kriol
Victoria Daly Regional Council
Stuart
Kybrook Farm is located just south of Pine Creek at the entrance to Umbrawarra Gorge Nature Park.

Name: LAJAMANU
Description:
The community is located approximately 560 kms south west of Katherine, on the northern edge of the Tanami Desert and the eastern side of Hooker Creek. Access is via the sealed Buntine Highway and then via 100kms of unsealed road. Access can also be made from Alice Springs utilising the Tanami Road, which is unsealed and often in poor repair. 
By road the travel time is 6 hours drive to Katherine.

Services.Comments: By road, Lajamanu can be accessed from Katherine and from Alice Springs. From Katherine, access is via the sealed Buntine Highway and then via approximately 100 km of unsealed road. The travel time is around 6 hours. Access can also be made from Alice Springs via the Tanami Road, which is currently sealed from Alice Springs to within 8 km from Yuendumu, then via the Lajamanu Road. The unsealed section of the Tanami Road as well as the unsealed Lajamanu Road are often in poor repair. The distance from Alice Springs is approx 880 km.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Lajamanu is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Lajamanu has good quality water with an adequate groundwater supply.
Lajamanu has a fully reticulated sewerage system.
Warlpiri
Central Desert Regional Council
Stuart

Lajamanu is located south west of Katherine on the northern edge of the Tanami Desert and the eastern side of Hooker Creek as part of the Hooker Creek Aboriginal Land Trust. Lajamanu also borders the southern boundary of Wave Hill Station.

PopulationIndicators.Label: Median age of persons
PopulationIndicators.Comments: Median age (in years) of the population at the time of the Census (excludes overseas visitors).

PopulationIndicators.Label: Median total personal income ($/weekly)
PopulationIndicators.Comments: Median total personal income ($/ weekly) at the time of the Census. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and over.

PopulationIndicators.Label: Median total family income ($/weekly)
PopulationIndicators.Comments: Median total family income ($/ weekly) at the time of the Census.

PopulationIndicators.Label: Median total household income ($/weekly)
PopulationIndicators.Comments: Median total household income ($/weekly) at the time of the Census. It excludes 'Visitors only' and 'Other non-classifiable' households.

PopulationIndicators.Label: Average number of persons per bedroom
PopulationIndicators.Comments: Average number of persons per bedroom at the time of the Census. It excludes 'Visitors only' and 'Other non-classifiable' households.

PopulationIndicators.Label: Average household size
PopulationIndicators.Comments: Average number of persons per household at the time of the Census. It excludes 'Visitors only' and 'Other non-classifiable' households.

PopulationIndicators.Label: Percent households where rent payments are more than 30% of household (RAID) income
PopulationIndicators.Comments: Proportion of households for whom rent payments were more than 30% of household income at the time of the Census.

LabourForceIndicators.Label: % Unemployment
LabourForceIndicators.Comments: Unemployment rate (%) at the time of the Census. This is the number of unemployed persons expressed as a percentage of the total labour force. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and older.

LabourForceIndicators.Label: % Labour force participation
LabourForceIndicators.Comments: Labour force participation rate (%) at the time of the Census. This is the number of unemployed persons expressed as a percentage of the total labour force. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and older.

LabourForceIndicators.Label: % Employment to population
LabourForceIndicators.Comments: Employment to population rate (%) at the time of the Census. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and older.

HealthCareIndicators.Label: Rates of core activity need for assistance
HealthCareIndicators.Comments: Number of people with a profound or severe core activity limitation. People with a profound or severe core activity limitation are those needing assistance in their day to day lives.

HealthCareIndicators.Label: Rates of long-term health conditions (per 1,000)
HealthCareIndicators.Comments: Rates of long-term health conditions (per 1, 000 population). This measures the number of people who reported that they have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have any of these long-term health conditions.

HealthCareIndicators.Label: Rates of caring (unpaid) for a person with a disability, health condition, or due to old age
HealthCareIndicators.Comments: Rates of unpaid caring provided to a person with a disability, health condition, or due to old age (%).

Name: LARRIMAH
Description: The Town is located 435km SSE of Darwin.
HistoryDesc:
The name Larrimah is believed to originate from the Yangman Aboriginal people. In the Yangman language, Larrimah translates to 'meeting place', reflecting the area's role as a gathering spot for various groups over time. 

Before European settlement, the Yangman people inhabited the region for over 40,000 years. They associate the landscape of Larrimah with the Dreaming tracks of the Storm Bird, also known as the channel-billed cuckoo, which they believe helped shape the land. 

The town of Larrimah itself was officially established in 1940 as the southern terminus of the North Australia Railway. During World War II, it became a significant military hub, serving as a staging point for troops and supplies. The nearby Gorrie Airfield, constructed during the war, further solidified Larrimah's strategic importance. 

Today, Larrimah remains a small community. 

Sources:

Therefore, the statistics shown here are for the entire region not for a single community.
AliasNameDescription: The community Larrimah is not known to have any other aliases.
HistoryDescription:
The name Larrimah is believed to originate from the Yangman Aboriginal people. In the Yangman language, Larrimah translates to 'meeting place', reflecting the area's role as a gathering spot for various groups over time. 

Before European settlement, the Yangman people inhabited the region for over 40,000 years. They associate the landscape of Larrimah with the Dreaming tracks of the Storm Bird, also known as the channel-billed cuckoo, which they believe helped shape the land. 

The town of Larrimah itself was officially established in 1940 as the southern terminus of the North Australia Railway. During World War II, it became a significant military hub, serving as a staging point for troops and supplies. The nearby Gorrie Airfield, constructed during the war, further solidified Larrimah's strategic importance. 

Today, Larrimah remains a small community.

Name: MANINGRIDA
Description: The community is located on the Central Arnhem coast at the mouth of the Liverpool River. It is 250km west of Nhulunbuy and 352km east of Darwin. From Darwin it takes around 6 - 10 hours in total (500km). This is about 3 hours on a sealed road between Darwin to East Alligator then 3-7 hours unsealed road on to Maningrida. It is a one hour flight from Darwin.
HistoryDesc:
The name Maningrida is an Anglicised version of the Kunibídji name Manayingkarírra, which comes from the phrase Mane djang karirra, meaning "the place where the Dreaming changed shape." The town supports a population of 2,600 people, which includes those who live on the 30 homeland centres or outstations around Maningrida. 

The township of Maningrida dates back to just after World War 2, when Welfare Branch patrol officers Sid Kyle-Little and Jack Doolan were sent by the government to set up a ration-cum-trade post there. This was converted by Dave and Ingrid Drysdale into a permanent Welfare Department settlement from 1957, partly to quell the post-war migration of Aboriginal people from the Blyth and Liverpool Rivers regions into Darwin. Patrols went out to spread the word and encourage people to move into the settlement. Within a few years, many people from the surrounding area were living in Maningrida.

Services.Comments: Access to Maningrida via a sealed road to Cahills Crossing, and a dirt road for a further 250 km (4WD recommended but not essential). During the wet season access is limited, with the road often closed for extended periods. The drive takes approximately seven hours from Darwin.

HistoryDescription:
The name Maningrida is an Anglicised version of the Kunibídji name Manayingkarírra, which comes from the phrase Mane djang karirra, meaning "the place where the Dreaming changed shape." The town supports a population of 2,600 people, which includes those who live on the 30 homeland centres or outstations around Maningrida. 

The township of Maningrida dates back to just after World War 2, when Welfare Branch patrol officers Sid Kyle-Little and Jack Doolan were sent by the government to set up a ration-cum-trade post there. This was converted by Dave and Ingrid Drysdale into a permanent Welfare Department settlement from 1957, partly to quell the post-war migration of Aboriginal people from the Blyth and Liverpool Rivers regions into Darwin. Patrols went out to spread the word and encourage people to move into the settlement. Within a few years, many people from the surrounding area were living in Maningrida.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Manyallaluk is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Manyallaluk has a plentiful groundwater source with very good quality water, which is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.

Houses and buildings in part of Manyallaluk have septic systems connected to a common effluent disposal system. Houses and buildings in the other part of the community are fitted with private septic systems.
Eastside Kriol
Roper Gulf Regional Council
Stuart
Manyallaluk is located north east of Katherine on the Manyallaluk Aboriginal Land Trust, just east of the Nitmiluk National Park boundary.

Name: MATARANKA
HistoryDesc: Mataranka is a name of Maori origin and was applied by Dr J A Gilruth about 1914-15 when establishing an Experimental Sheep Farm near the Thermal Springs area. When the rail line was extended to the present Town area in 1928, the Town of Mataranka was officially gazetted on 24/05/1928 (CG48) comprising 510 hectares. Mataranka became a Community Government Centre on 23/05/1985.

HistoryDescription: Mataranka is a name of Maori origin and was applied by Dr J A Gilruth about 1914-15 when establishing an Experimental Sheep Farm near the Thermal Springs area. When the rail line was extended to the present Town area in 1928, the Town of Mataranka was officially gazetted on 24/05/1928 (CG48) comprising 510 hectares. Mataranka became a Community Government Centre on 23/05/1985.

Projects.Description: THE TIWI ISLANDS IPA CONSULTATION PROJECT WILL CONSULT WITH TRADITIONAL OWNERS, NEIGHBOURING LAND OWNERS AND STATUTORY LAND MANAGEMENT AUTHORITIES TO DEVELOP AN IPA PROPOSAL. A PLAN OF MANAGEMENT AND ASSOCIATED MERI FRAMEWORK WILL BE DEVELOPED FOR THE PROPOSED IPA IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE &LSQUO;OUR COUNTRY OUR WAY: GUIDELINES 2016 &RSQUO; FOR AUSTRALIAN IPA MANAGEMENT PLANS AND IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PROTECTED AREA MANAGEMENT CATEGORIES OUTLINED BY THE INTERNATIONAL UNION FOR CONSERVATION OF NATURE (IUCN). THE CONSULTATIONS WILL INFORM TRADITIONAL OWNERS AND OTHER RELEVANT STAKEHOLDERS ABOUT THE LONG-TERM ENVIRONMENTAL AND CULTURAL HERITAGE MANAGEMENT OF THE LAND AND SEA OF THE TIWI ISLANDS IN THE NORTHERN TERRITORY AND SUPPORT A DECISION ON WHETHER THE AREA SHOULD BE DEDICATED AS AN IPA.

Name: MILINGIMBI
Description:
The community is the main settlement on Milingimbi Island which forms part of the Crocodile Island Group, located approximately half a km off the north coast of Central Arnhem Land in the Arafura Sea.  Milingimbi is approximately 440 km east of Darwin and 206 km west of Nhulunbuy.

Apart from the weekly freight barge service from Darwin, Milingimbi is generally accessed by air.  Milingimbi has a sealed, all weather air strip. Travel time to Darwin: 2-3hrs, to Nhulunbuy: 45 mins-1hr.

Services.Comments:
Airnorth and Fly Tiwi offer flights from Darwin.

Mission Aviation Fellowship offers flights from Nhulunbuy.

Sealed - approximate distance 3 km (5min drive) from the community.

The Malmaldharra Health Centre (Milingimbi Clinic) is operated by the Miwatj Health Aboriginal Corporation (08) 8987 9903.

Operating hours Monday to Friday 8:30am-4:30pm, but with Wednesday being 8:30am - 1pm.

In an emergency call 000. No immediate danger call 131 444.

For general enquiries during business hours, call the station at (08) 8987 9874.

Milingimbi Community Education Centre is a bilingual school operated by the Department of Education (8987 9902) and is a Limited program school for ABSTUDY and Youth Allowance, for more information. It offers a FaFT program (0-5 years), and Preschool through to Year 12.
Milingimbi Library is situated within the Milingimbi school and is run by the East Arnhem Regional Council. Its is open Monday to Friday 9am - 12pm and 1pm- 4pm.
East Arnhem Regional Council - Milingimbi Office (08) 8970 1702

The primary employment and remote training services provider in Milingimbi is ALPA (The Arnhem Land Progress Aboriginal Corporation), located at Lot 209 Milingimbi Community (08 8944 5950). They deliver the Remote Australia Employment Service (RAES) and the Indigenous Skills and Employment Program (ISEP) to support local job seekers and career development.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Milingimbi is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Milingimbi has very good quality water, however the groundwater source is very limited and community demand is continuously monitored to ensure that adequate supply can be maintained.
Milingimbi has a fully reticulated sewerage system.
Yolngu Matha (Djambarrpuyngu)
Gapupuyngu
East Arnhem Regional Council
Arnhem

Milingimbi Island forms part of the Crocodile Island Group off the north coast of Central Arnhem Land in the Arafura Sea west of Nhulunbuy. Milingimbi is part of the Arnhem Land Aboriginal Land Trust.

Name: MILYAKBURRA
Description:
The community is situated on the central eastern section of Bickerton Island.  Bickerton Island is situated 13 km west off Groote Eylandt and 8 km east of mainland Australia, between Groote Eylandt and Blue Mud Bay north of Numbulwar.

Milyakburra is approximately one hour by boat from Alyangula on Groote Eylandt.  However, apart from the fortnightly freight barge service from Darwin, Milyakburra is generally accessed by air.  A dirt airstrip is located within 5 minutes walk of the community and can accommodate twin engine light aircraft.  Travel time to Alyangula 15 mins, Nhulunbuy 30-40 minutes.

Services.Comments:
Milyakburra (Bickerton Island) is based off of Groote Eylandt and within the Groote Archipelago.


Airnorth flies to Groote Eylandt Aerodrome (Angurugu).


Chartair provides a weekly Remote Air Services Subsidy service and bookings can be made by phoning Chartair on 1300 790 800 or online at Scheduled Flights Northern Territory | Chartair

Milyakburra on Bickerton Island does not have a permanent, full-time resident police station. Instead, the community receives periodic visits and coverage from the Northern Territory Police based out of Groote Eylandt (primarily managed via the Alyangula Police Station) (8987 6122)

Milyakburra School has Preschool, Primary School, Middle School, Senior School.

The boarding school on Bickerton Island (Wurriyukwayuwa-Langwa College) will be an independent, bilingual boarding school which is expected to be open by Term 2, 2027.

Minjilang has a plentiful groundwater source with very good quality water, which is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Minjilang has a fully reticulated sewerage system.

Name: MINYERRI
Description: The community is located approximately 270 km south-east of Katherine by road. The Hodgson River is in close proximity.
HistoryDesc:
In 1990, the (former) Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Commission (ATSIC) purchased the Hodgson Downs Station, now known as Warrigundu Station, for the Alawa Traditional Owners. 

Following acquisition of the station, many residents returned to Minyerri, which is located near the station homestead. 

The community gives its name to the gazetted locality Miniyeri (see place ID 22441). The origin of the variation in spelling for the locality name is unknown.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Minyerri is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.

Minyerri has marginal quality water due to poor aesthetic characteristics, including elevated levels of iron, manganese and turbidity. Capacity of the groundwater supply is limited and community demand is continuously monitored to ensure that adequate supply can be maintained.
Minyerri has a fully reticulated sewerage system.
Eastside Kriol
Roper Gulf Regional Council
Barkly
Minyerri is located south east of Katherine on the Alawa 1 Aboriginal Land Trust just west of the Hodgson River.

AliasNameDescription: Hodgson Downs, Miniyerre, Minyere, Minyeri and Minyerre
HistoryDescription:
In 1990, the (former) Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Commission (ATSIC) purchased the Hodgson Downs Station, now known as Warrigundu Station, for the Alawa Traditional Owners. 

Following acquisition of the station, many residents returned to Minyerri, which is located near the station homestead. 

The community gives its name to the gazetted locality Miniyeri (see place ID 22441). The origin of the variation in spelling for the locality name is unknown.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Mount Liebig is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Mt Liebig has limited groundwater source with marginal quality water, which is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Houses and buildings at Mount Liebig are fitted with private septic systems.
Luritja/Pintupi
MacDonnell Regional Council
Namatjira
Mount Liebig is located west of Alice Springs on the Haasts Bluff Aboriginal Land Trust at the western end of the Western McDonnell Ranges.

LabourForceIndicators.Comments: Labour force participation rate (%) at the time of the Census. This is the number of unemployed persons expressed as a percentage of the total labour force. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and older.

Projects.Title: INCENTIVISING ON COUNTRY ABORIGINAL EMPLOYMENT: ANANGU FUTURES.
Projects.Description: THIS PROJECT AIMS TO INVESTIGATE THE CHANGING FACE OF CULTURAL TOURISM IN CENTRAL AUSTRALIA AND EXAMINE PATHWAYS TOWARDS SUSTAINABLE ABORIGINAL EMPLOYMENT IN AND AROUND ULURU-KATA TJUTA NATIONAL PARK. THE PROJECT IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT BRINGS TOGETHER ABORIGINAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS, INDUSTRY AND GOVERNMENT STAKEHOLDERS TO IDENTIFY MICRO-BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES, YOUTH TRAINING INITIATIVES, BETTER RELATIONS ACROSS CULTURAL DIVIDES, AND THE ECONOMIC VALUE OF ABORIGINAL KNOWLEDGE. OUTCOMES INCLUDE A MODEL FOR SUSTAINABLE ABORIGINAL EMPLOYMENT IN REMOTE AND VERY REMOTE CONTEXTS, AND  THE DEVELOPMENT OF CULTURALLY RELEVANT AND SUSTAINABLE GOVERNING GUIDELINES FOR REGIONAL INVESTMENT. BENEFITS INCLUDE MORE SUSTAINABLE JOBS FOR ABORIGINAL PEOPLE.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity supply at Mutitjulu is provided by Parks Australia.
Mutitjulu water supply is provided by Parks Australia. The groundwater supply is adequate but generally characterised by hardness, and high total dissolved solids affecting colour and taste.
Mutitjulu has a reticulated sewerage system provided by Parks Australia.
Pitjantjatjara
Luritja/Pintupi
MacDonnell Regional Council
Namatjira
Mutitjulu is located at the base of Uluru (also known as Ayers Rock) within the Uluru-Katatjuta National Park, south west of Alice Springs.

LabourForceIndicators.Label: % Unemployment
LabourForceIndicators.Comments: Unemployment rate (%) at the time of the Census. This is the number of unemployed persons expressed as a percentage of the total labour force. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and older.

LabourForceIndicators.Label: % Labour force participation
LabourForceIndicators.Comments: Labour force participation rate (%) at the time of the Census. This is the number of unemployed persons expressed as a percentage of the total labour force. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and older.

LabourForceIndicators.Label: % Employment to population
LabourForceIndicators.Comments: Employment to population rate (%) at the time of the Census. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and older.

HealthCareIndicators.Label: Rates of core activity need for assistance
HealthCareIndicators.Comments: Number of people with a profound or severe core activity limitation. People with a profound or severe core activity limitation are those needing assistance in their day to day lives.

HealthCareIndicators.Comments: Rates of long-term health conditions (per 1, 000 population). This measures the number of people who reported that they have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have any of these long-term health conditions.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Nauiyu is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Nauiyu has a plentiful groundwater source with marginal quality water, which is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Nauiyu has a fully reticulated sewerage system.

Nauiyu is located south of Darwin on the banks of the Daly River.

Name: NEWCASTLE WATERS
Description: Newcastle Waters Town is an excision of the Newcastle Waters Cattle Station. It is located approximately 25 km north of Elliott. Newcastle Waters is an historic 10,353 square kilometre cattle station in the Barkly Tablelands. This huge station is located 777 kilometres north of Alice Springs, 290kms North of Tennant Creek and 705 kilometres south from Darwin and was once the drover's crossing point where stock routes from the east and south met.
HistoryDesc:
This population centre and old drovers town takes its name from the adjacent water body named by John McDouall Stuart in 1861 after the Duke of Newcastle, Henry Pelham.  

McDouall Stuart's original handwritten journal shows that he actually named the water body, Glandfield Lagoon after the then Major of Adelaide, but the SA Government decided to apply the name, Newcastle Waters, after the Secretary for Colonies.  

After the Pastoral Station was established here about 1885 and later operated by the Lewis family etc, the Federal Government constructed a Police Station and other facilities before WW2 at the junction of the Stock Routes.  Finally, a town area (on the "Ridge") was surveyed and gazetted (CG 2, 9 January 1964; NTG 3, 22/1/64) containing 23.59 hectares.  

It lies 285 kilometres north north west of Tennant Creek.

Name: NGANMARRIYANGA
Description: The community is located on Palumpa Station In Daly River Reserve 240km southwest of Darwin. By road it is 375km from Darwin via the Daly River crossing. The last 142km of the journey is dirt.  The community is cut off during the wet season from about late November to April/May. During this time travel is limited to air. The road between Palumpa and Port Keats, though only 45km away, is impassable during the wet season.
HistoryDesc:
Name change from Palumpa at the request of the Cmty Council.  Palumpa is the adjoining cattle station.

Nganmarriyanga is pronounced "Nan-marri-yanga" or "None-murray-yunga".

Nganmarriyanga community was founded by the Wodidj family.  In the period of initial contact with non-Aboriginal people before World War 2, this family group left the area as the men sought employment on cattle stations in northern Western Australia. They returned to nearby Port Keats Mission (now Wadeye) some time after the war with the knowledge that their father s country was some distance away. They moved back to that area and began to build a community known as Palumpa. They cut local timber for houses and yards, built fences, hand dug trenches to pipe water from nearby creeks and ran cattle. These were sold to Port Keats and other nearby communities. 
 
For a long time Palumpa Station was the only provider of services to the developing community of people. During the 1980s, as more people came to live at Palumpa, it was decided that the Station alone could not support the population.  In 1985 Palumpa (later Nganmarriyanga) Community Inc. was formed as a local governing body for the community and funds were attracted for the purpose of building community infrastructure. 
 
Palumpa Station has continued as a Proprietary Limited company, whose Directors largely represent the traditional owners of the area. The Station has grown as a viable industry and has recently completed construction of a state of the art Abattoir. Palumpa Station remains a major employer of local Aboriginal men in the area. The Station also operates the Workshop for mechanical repairs to vehicles and equipment and fuel distribution to the community. 
 
The Council is an incorporated association responsible for the delivery of local government services to almost 500 indigenous residents.  
 
In 2006, the Nganmarriyanga Community Inc owns and manages 43 community houses, 4 Staff houses, Contractor's Quarters, Community Centre and Store. There are also administration buildings including a Council Office, Parks and Gardens shed and a Housing Maintenance workshop. All properties within the community are serviced by power, water and sewer. The majority of the internal road network is sealed and there are well established parks and gardens. 
 
The community is serviced by a Primary School operated by the NT Department of Education. The School is a modern well-equipped complex located in the centre of the community.  
  
The community Health Clinic is operated by Territory Health Services.
The Health Centre is a modern facility that was constructed in 1998.

Services.Comments: By road the community is 375 km from Darwin on the Port Keats Road between the communities of Peppimenarti and Wadeye. The Palumpa access road is unsealed and approx 140 km from the Daly River Bridge. The community is cut off during the wet season for extended period. The road between Palumpa and Port Keats, though only 45km away, is also impassable during the wet season.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Nganmarriyanga is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Nganmarriyanga has a plentiful groundwater source with very good quality water, which is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Nganmarriyanga has a septic tank effluent pumping system for the transfer of effluent to sewer ponds from septic tanks on houses and buildings.
Murrinh Patha
West Daly Regional Council
Daly
Nganmarriyanga is located south west of Darwin on the Daly River/Port Keats Aboriginal Land Trust.

HistoryDescription:
Name change from Palumpa at the request of the Cmty Council.  Palumpa is the adjoining cattle station.

Nganmarriyanga is pronounced "Nan-marri-yanga" or "None-murray-yunga".

Nganmarriyanga community was founded by the Wodidj family.  In the period of initial contact with non-Aboriginal people before World War 2, this family group left the area as the men sought employment on cattle stations in northern Western Australia. They returned to nearby Port Keats Mission (now Wadeye) some time after the war with the knowledge that their father s country was some distance away. They moved back to that area and began to build a community known as Palumpa. They cut local timber for houses and yards, built fences, hand dug trenches to pipe water from nearby creeks and ran cattle. These were sold to Port Keats and other nearby communities. 
 
For a long time Palumpa Station was the only provider of services to the developing community of people. During the 1980s, as more people came to live at Palumpa, it was decided that the Station alone could not support the population.  In 1985 Palumpa (later Nganmarriyanga) Community Inc. was formed as a local governing body for the community and funds were attracted for the purpose of building community infrastructure. 
 
Palumpa Station has continued as a Proprietary Limited company, whose Directors largely represent the traditional owners of the area. The Station has grown as a viable industry and has recently completed construction of a state of the art Abattoir. Palumpa Station remains a major employer of local Aboriginal men in the area. The Station also operates the Workshop for mechanical repairs to vehicles and equipment and fuel distribution to the community. 
 
The Council is an incorporated association responsible for the delivery of local government services to almost 500 indigenous residents.  
 
In 2006, the Nganmarriyanga Community Inc owns and manages 43 community houses, 4 Staff houses, Contractor's Quarters, Community Centre and Store. There are also administration buildings including a Council Office, Parks and Gardens shed and a Housing Maintenance workshop. All properties within the community are serviced by power, water and sewer. The majority of the internal road network is sealed and there are well established parks and gardens. 
 
The community is serviced by a Primary School operated by the NT Department of Education. The School is a modern well-equipped complex located in the centre of the community.  
  
The community Health Clinic is operated by Territory Health Services.
The Health Centre is a modern facility that was constructed in 1998.

Description:
The community is located about 320km south east of Katherine on the banks of the Roper River. 
By road it takes approximately 3.5 hours from Katherine.

Services.Comments: Welcome to our Country

Access to Ngukurr by road uses the Roper Highway which is single and double lane bitumen. The last 70km into Ngukurr is well maintained gravel, which can be used by conventional cars during the dry season and 4WD during the wet season. Travel time by road is approximately 3.5 hours from Katherine. New bridges built over the Roper and Wilton Rivers reduce the impact of severe flooding. When flooded, the road is inaccessible.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Ngukurr is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.

Ngukurr has marginal quality water due to poor aesthetic characteristics, including elevated levels of hardness, and high levels of total dissolved solids affecting colour and taste. Capacity of the groundwater supply is limited and community demand is continuously monitored to ensure that adequate supply can be maintained.
Ngukurr has a fully reticulated sewerage system.

Roper Gulf Regional Council
Arnhem
Ngukurr is located on the banks of the Roper River south east of Katherine and is part of the Arnhem Land Aboriginal Land Trust.

Name: NHULUNBUY
Description:
The Town is located about 1000 kms from Darwin. It is 700 kilometres to Katherine by road. This road is a dirt track, which is only open during the dry season, ie. April to October, for 4 wheel drive vehicles ONLY. A permit is required from the Northern Lands Council Office to travel on this road.
The community can be accessed all year round by air, providing weather conditions are favourable. As with all top end communities, the area is prone to cyclones, and monsoonal rains between November to April.
HistoryDesc:
Nhulunbuy is a private mining town residing on Aboriginal Land. Nhulunbuy was established in the 1960s by Nabalco Pty Ltd on land adjacent to Mount Saunders (named by Matthew Flinders in 1803) to service the nearby bauxite deposit on Gove Peninsula.

It was originally recommended the town be named Gove, and as such was gazetted on 21 August 1968. Refer to Place ID 13240 Gove (Town). 

However, Prime Minister John G Gorton whilst visiting the Northern Territory decided on and announced the name of the town would be "Nhulunbuy" in lieu of Gove after a delegation from Yirrkala who believed Nhulunbuy was the name given to the township area by Wuyal, one of their dream-time ancestors, being "Nhulun" - the traditional name for Mount Saunders and "buy" - adjoining area or associated with. The town was officially renamed Nhulunbuy in 2007.

The tenure of the town is somewhat complex.  The Nhulunbuy Corporation Ltd has controlled the Special Purpose town since 1972.

Projects.Title: ENSURING PROVISION OF ESSENTIAL PRIMARY HEALTH CARE SERVICES
Projects.Description: THE COMMONWEALTH HEALTH WORKFORCE PROGRAM DELIVERS HEATH WORKFORCE OUTCOMES AND SUPPORT FOR RURAL OUTREACH HEALTH SERVICES. THE HEALTH WORKFORCE PROGRAM IS DELIVERED UNDER THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND AGED CARE&RSQUO;S OUTCOME 1.4 &NDASH; HEALTH WORKFORCE. THIS OUTCOME IS INTENDED TO IMPROVE IMPROVE THE QUALITY, DISTRIBUTION AND PLANNING OF THE AUSTRALIAN HEALTH WORKFORCE TO BETTER MEET THE NEEDS OF THE COMMUNITY AND DELIVER A SUSTAINABLE, WELL DISTRIBUTED HEALTH WORKFORCE. IN THE 2022-23 BUDGET, THE AUSTRALIAN GOVERNMENT ANNOUNCED A LANDMARK LONG-TERM ENGAGEMENT WITH THE ROYAL FLYING DOCTOR SERVICE (RFDS OF AUSTRALIA). THIS ANNOUNCEMENT COMPRISES OF THIS &LSQUO;ENSURING PROVISION OF ESSENTIAL PRIMARY HEALTH CARE SERVICES IN RURAL AND REMOTE AUSTRALIA&RSQUO; PROGRAM, A 10-YEAR STRATEGIC AGREEMENT AND UP TO APPROXIMATELY $1 BILLION OVER A PERIOD OF UP TO TEN YEARS TO PROVIDE ESSENTIAL PRIMARY HEALTH CARE SERVICES AND AEROMEDICAL EVACUATIONS FOR RURAL AND REMOTE PATIENTS IN AREAS OF MARKET FAILURE OR BEYOND WHERE NORMAL MEDICAL INFRASTRUCTURE WOULD OTHERWISE PROVIDE SERVICES. THIS INCLUDES REFORM OF THE COMMONWEALTH&RSQUO;S PARTNERSHIP WITH THE RFDS OF AUSTRALIA TO INCLUDE COLLABORATIVE ANNUAL SERVICE PLANNING, AND INCREASED FLEXIBILITY AND RESPONSIVENESS IN FUNDING ALLOCATION AND SERVICE LEVELS TO ENSURE HEALTH SERVICES ARE DELIVERED TO THOSE COMMUNITIES MOST IN NEED, IN RURAL AND REMOTE AUSTRALIA.&NBSP;&NBSP;

Projects.Title: DHUPUMA BARKER - VEX ROBOTICS WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS
Projects.Description: EIGHT INDIGENOUS YOLNGU STUDENTS FROM DHUPUMA BARKER COMPETED IN THE NATIONAL VEX ROBOTICS IN DECEMBER 2022, FINISHING 4TH IN THE COUNTRY. THEY HAVE NOW QUALIFIED FOR THE WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS TO BE HELD IN DALLAS TEXAS USA IN APRIL/MAY 2023. THIS IS THE FIRST TEAM TO EVER REPRESENT STUDENTS FROM A VERY REMOTE COMMUNITY, THE NT AND NOW THEIR COUNTRY. THE STUDENTS HAD ONLY BEEN INTRODUCED TO STEM THROUGH ROBOTICS IN JULY 2022, AND WITH ONLY A FEW SHORT WEEKS OF TRAINING, HAVE FLOURISHED TO BECOME NATION LEADERS. THIS IS AN EXCEPTIONAL OUTCOME FOR THE STUDENTS WHO NOW INSPIRE ALL INDIGENOUS STUDENTS FROM ACROSS AUSTRALIA TO ENGAGE IN STEM LEARNING THROUGH ROBOTICS.

Projects.Description: PACIFICAUS SPORTS&RSQUO; PURPOSE IS TO STRENGTHEN PEOPLE-TO-PEOPLE LINKS BETWEEN AUSTRALIA AND THE PACIFIC THROUGH SPORT TO ENHANCE AUSTRALIA&RSQUO;S RELATIONSHIPS AND STANDING IN THE PACIFIC. PACIFICAUS SPORTS DOES THIS BY FOSTERING ELITE SPORT PATHWAYS AND LINKAGES THAT FACILITATE REGULAR COMPETITION AND ENGAGEMENT BETWEEN AUSTRALIA AND PACIFIC TEAMS, ATHLETES AND OTHER SPORT STAKEHOLDERS. THE OBJECTIVES OF PACIFICAUS SPORTS PARTNERSHIP GRANTS ARE: (1) DEVELOPING PATHWAYS FOR PACIFIC TEAMS AND ATHLETES TO PLAY IN HIGH LEVEL AUSTRALIAN SPORTS COMPETITIONS: (2) SUPPORTING AUSTRALIAN SPORTS CODES TO INCREASE THEIR PRESENCE AND PARTICIPATION IN THE PACIFIC; AND (3) DEVELOPING PATHWAYS FOR EMERGING ATHLETES FROM THE REGION TO BENEFIT FROM HIGH PERFORMANCE COACHING, TRAINING, AND COMPETITION. THIS GRANT WILL ENABLE NETBALL AUSTRALIA TO CONTRIBUTE TO THESE OBJECTIVES USING NETBALL THROUGH ACTIVITIES INCLUDING SUPPORT FOR PACIFIC TEAMS AND PLAYERS TO COMPETE AND TRAIN IN AUSTRALIA, SUPPORT FOR AUSTRALIAN NETBALL CLUBS TO ENGAGE WITH THE PACIFIC, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF HIGH PERFORMANCE WORKSHOPS AND COACHING DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS.

AliasNameDescription: The community Nhulunbuy is not known to have any other aliases.
HistoryDescription:
Nhulunbuy is a private mining town residing on Aboriginal Land. Nhulunbuy was established in the 1960s by Nabalco Pty Ltd on land adjacent to Mount Saunders (named by Matthew Flinders in 1803) to service the nearby bauxite deposit on Gove Peninsula.

It was originally recommended the town be named Gove, and as such was gazetted on 21 August 1968. Refer to Place ID 13240 Gove (Town). 

However, Prime Minister John G Gorton whilst visiting the Northern Territory decided on and announced the name of the town would be "Nhulunbuy" in lieu of Gove after a delegation from Yirrkala who believed Nhulunbuy was the name given to the township area by Wuyal, one of their dream-time ancestors, being "Nhulun" - the traditional name for Mount Saunders and "buy" - adjoining area or associated with. The town was officially renamed Nhulunbuy in 2007.

The tenure of the town is somewhat complex.  The Nhulunbuy Corporation Ltd has controlled the Special Purpose town since 1972.

Name: NITJPURRU
Description: The community is located 300km SSW of Katherine.  The Essential services for the community are accessed from Yarralin 70kms away.
HistoryDesc:
Formerly known as Pigeon Hole, in 2024 the community name changed to its Bilinarra language name - Nitjpurru - at the request of the Traditional Owners. 

Nitjpurru is the traditional name for the billabong just north of where the community is situated. 

The previous name Pigeon Hole initially described the former outstation on the Victoria River Downs pastoral lease that surrounds the present community.

HistoryDescription:
Formerly known as Pigeon Hole, in 2024 the community name changed to its Bilinarra language name - Nitjpurru - at the request of the Traditional Owners. 

Nitjpurru is the traditional name for the billabong just north of where the community is situated. 

The previous name Pigeon Hole initially described the former outstation on the Victoria River Downs pastoral lease that surrounds the present community.

Name: NUMBULWAR
Description:
The community is located at the mouth of the Rose River on the western coast of the Gulf of Carpentaria, and adjacent to the extreme SW coast of Groote Eylandt.  Numbulwar is approximately 400 km east of Katherine, 570 km south east of Darwin and 250 km south west of Nhulunbuy.

During the dry season the community can be accessed by road.  Travel time from Darwin via Katherine along the Roper Highway is approximately 10-12 hours via the Roper River and Ngukurr communities.  Travel time from Nhulunbuy via Walker River and Harris Creek is approximately 4-6 hours.  In both cases a 4wd is essential.  Numbulwar is also accessible by air and has an all weather, sealed airstrip linked to the community via a 5 km dirt road which can become impassable at times during the wet season.  Travel time to Alyangula, Groote Eylandt: 30 min, to Nhulunbuy 1 hour.  There is a fortnightly freight barge service from Darwin to Numbulwar.

Services.Comments: Welcome to our Country

Numbulwar is approx 438 km East of Katherine. The community is accessible by road mostly during the dry season only from Katherine via the Roper River and Ngukurr communities. Travelling is difficult due to significant dirt sections with corrugations and water crossings. Roads may only be open for 4-5 months every year and then in varying conditions.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Numbulwar is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Numbulwar has marginal quality water due to poor aesthetic characteristics, including  elevated levels of iron, turbidity and some hardness. Capacity of the groundwater supply is adequate.
Numbulwar  has a fully reticulated sewerage system.
Eastside Kriol
Nunggubuyu
Roper Gulf Regional Council
Arnhem

Numbulwar is located at the mouth of Rose River on the western coast of the Gulf of Carpentaria, and adjacent to the extreme SW coast of Groote Eylandt. Numbulwar is part of the Arnhem Land Aboriginal Land Trust.

Name: NYIRRIPI
Description:
The community is located approximately 440 km from Alice Springs by road and it takes 5? to 6 hours to drive there.  
There are two main routes. For the first route, travel from Alice Springs to Yuendumu via the Tanami Highway. The road is sealed for the first 190 km from the highway and the rest of the way is formed and largely gravelled with some sections not gravelled.  From Yuendumu, Nyirripi is approximately 150 kilometres west-southwest. The turn off for the community is approximately 1 kilometre on the left from the Yuendumu turn off. The access road is 150 km of formed track, which is passable except in extreme wet conditions. This distance can generally be covered in about 2 hours.

The second route also travels along the Tanami Highway until 23 kilometres past Tilmouth Wells roadhouse. Take the turn left on the Mt Wedge road, continue west on to Nyirripi.

Services.Comments: From Alice Springs travel via the Tanami Highway to Yuendumu, (293 km, 285 km sealed). Turn left opposite Yuendumu via the Nyirripi Road. Nyirripi is 150 km of dirt road. Always check the road conditions prior to travel. The Tilmouth Well Roadhouse is 188 km from Alice Springs for fuel and food.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Nyirripi is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Nyirripi has a limited groundwater source with marginal quality water, which is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Nyirripi has a fully reticulated sewerage system.
Warlpiri
Central Desert Regional Council
Stuart
Nyirripi is located close to the southern and south western extent of traditionally owned Warlpiri land on the Yunkanjini Aboriginal Land Trust between Newhaven and Mount Doreen Pastoral Properties.

Name: PALMERSTON
HistoryDesc:
Palmerston a satelite town of Darwin is located some 21km east of the city.

With the need to develop additional residential land, the government acquired the area on which the current town of Palmerston is built.  The Town of Palmerston was officially named in May 1981, with construction commencing in 1984.

Following the exceptional growth of the town, in early 2000 the Palmerston Town Council sought and obtained a change in the name of the municipality to "City of Palmerston" (NTG S41 of 2 August 2000).

In the 1870s, the name Palmerston was given to the early settlement at Port Darwin to honour the Prime Minister of Britian, Lord Palmerston, Henry Temple.

Since all communications with the settlement were by sea, goods and passengers continued to be consigned to PORT DARWIN although the settlement was named Palmerston. Some forty years later, in 1911, when the Commonwealth relieved the State of South Australia of the economic burden the Territory had become, Darwin was adopted as the official name of the capital and PALMERSTON was forgotten.

Projects.Description:

HistoryDescription:
Palmerston a satelite town of Darwin is located some 21km east of the city.

With the need to develop additional residential land, the government acquired the area on which the current town of Palmerston is built.  The Town of Palmerston was officially named in May 1981, with construction commencing in 1984.

Following the exceptional growth of the town, in early 2000 the Palmerston Town Council sought and obtained a change in the name of the municipality to "City of Palmerston" (NTG S41 of 2 August 2000).

In the 1870s, the name Palmerston was given to the early settlement at Port Darwin to honour the Prime Minister of Britian, Lord Palmerston, Henry Temple.

Since all communications with the settlement were by sea, goods and passengers continued to be consigned to PORT DARWIN although the settlement was named Palmerston. Some forty years later, in 1911, when the Commonwealth relieved the State of South Australia of the economic burden the Territory had become, Darwin was adopted as the official name of the capital and PALMERSTON was forgotten.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Papunya is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Papunya has plentiful groundwater source with marginal quality water, which is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Papunya has a septic tank effluent pumping system for the transfer of effluent to sewer ponds from septic tanks on houses and buildings.

LabourForceIndicators.Label: % Unemployment
LabourForceIndicators.Comments: Unemployment rate (%) at the time of the Census. This is the number of unemployed persons expressed as a percentage of the total labour force. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and older.

LabourForceIndicators.Label: % Labour force participation
LabourForceIndicators.Comments: Labour force participation rate (%) at the time of the Census. This is the number of unemployed persons expressed as a percentage of the total labour force. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and older.

LabourForceIndicators.Label: % Employment to population
LabourForceIndicators.Comments: Employment to population rate (%) at the time of the Census. Applicable to persons aged 15 years and older.

HealthCareIndicators.Label: Rates of core activity need for assistance
HealthCareIndicators.Comments: Number of people with a profound or severe core activity limitation. People with a profound or severe core activity limitation are those needing assistance in their day to day lives.

HealthCareIndicators.Comments: Rates of long-term health conditions (per 1, 000 population). This measures the number of people who reported that they have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have any of these long-term health conditions.

Name: PEPPIMENARTI
Description: The community is situated on Tom Turner creek, approximately 320km south west of Darwin. It is 120km west of the Daly River crossing, along the Port Keats road.

Services.Comments: Red Dust

The community located approx 320 km south east of Darwin, is accessible by road. It is 120 km west of the Daly River crossing, along the Port Keats road. The access road consists of both sealed (upto Daly River Crossing) and unsealed sections. During the wet season the unsealed section of the road becomes impassable and access often limited to plane.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Peppimenarti is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Peppimenarti has a plentiful groundwater with marginal quality water, which is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Peppimenarti has a septic tank effluent pumping system for the transfer of effluent to sewer ponds from septic tanks on houses and buildings.
Ngan'gikurunggurr
Kriol, Murrinh Patha
West Daly Regional Council
Daly
Peppimenarti is located south west of Darwin on the edge of Tom Turners Creek on the Daly River/Port Keats Aboriginal Land Trust.

Name: PINE CREEK
Description: The Town is located 220 km south of Darwin and 90km north of Katherine at the junction of the Stuart and Kakadu Highways in the Top End of Australia's Northern Territory. The travel time is about 2 hours from Darwin and about 1 hour from Katherine.
HistoryDesc:
The town of Pine Creek is named after the stream on the banks of which it is built and was originally officially called Playford, a name not commonly known except by officials.

Following the construction of the Overland Telegraph Line in 1871 and the subsequent discovery of gold, a Telegraph Station and Police Station were established adjacent to the Creek.

The North Australian Railway reached its terminus at Pine Creek in May 1889.

SW Herbert in his unpublished journal "Reminiscences of life in the Northern Territory: 1870-1873" writes:  "We setled down in our new camp at Pine Creek, since well known throughout Australia, first on account of its being a rich gold field, and years later as the inland terminus of our only railway on the north coast. The North Australian Railway reached its terminus at Pine Creek in May 1889.

SW Herbert in his unpublished journal "Reminiscences of life in the Northern Territory: 1870-1873" writes:  "We setled down in our new camp at Pine Creek, since well known throughout Australia, first on account of its being a rich gold field, and years later as the inland terminus of our only railway on the north coast. This creek is by no means large, but was remarkable for pines growing there, thus the name of Pine Creek.".

The Town of Playford was gazetted originally vide SA Gazette of 24 January 1889 after Thomas Playford Senior, former South Australian Premier.  It was finally regazetted as the Town of Pine Creek, as it always had been known for the pine trees which once grew in the Creek, on 20 September 1973 (CG 129) and extended vide NTG 38, 23 September 1983.  

Pine Creek embraced local government  on 15 May 1987 as the Pine Creek Community Government Council.

HistoryDescription: Pirlangimpi,  on Melville Island, was established as a Mission by the Catholic Church in 1940 and known as Garden Point.  In 1979, following a request from the traditional owners, the Community was renamed Pularumpi and more recently to Pirlangimpi.

Name: PMARA JUTUNTA
Description:
The community is located 190km north of Alice Springs by road travelling on the Stuart Highway and it takes 2 hours to drive there.  By road, it takes 10 minutes to drive to the closest airstrip in Ti Tree Town then 30 minutes to fly to Alice Springs.

The community is situated approximately 500 metres to the east of the Stuart Highway.  Located between the community and the highway are the water bores and storage reservoirs, secured by a high chain wire fence.

Name: RAMINGINING
Description:
The community is located on the edge of the heritage listed Arafura Wetlands in Central Arnhem Land.  Ramingining is located approximately 580 km east of Darwin, 435 km west of Nhulunbuy and 30 km inland from the coast.

Whilst the community is accessible by road (4wd) and air, all roads to the community are closed during the wet season.  Travel time by road to Darwin and Nhulunbuy is 8 hours.  Ramingining has a sealed, all weather air strip.  Travel time by air to Darwin: 2.5 hrs, to Nhulunbuy: 45-50 mins.  There is a weekly freight barge service from Darwin to Ramingining via the Glyde River.

Services.Comments: Welcome to Ramingining - Do's & Dont's

The community is 435 km west of Nhulunbuy by road. It is accessible by road (4wd) however, all roads to the community are closed during the wet season. Travel time by road to Darwin and Nhulunbuy is 8 hours. Travel time from Nhulunbuy is approximately 6-8 hours depending on road/weather conditions.
Check Road Report NT and Check the tides before travelling

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Ramingining is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Ramingining has very good quality water with an adequate groundwater supply.
Ramingining has a fully reticulated sewerage system.
Yolngu Matha (Djambarrpuyngu)
Gupapuyngu , Djinang
East Arnhem Regional Council
Arnhem
Ramingining is located on the edge of the heritage listed Arafura Wetlands in Central Arnhem Land west of Nhulunbuy. Ramingining is part of the Arnhem Land Aboriginal Land Trust.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Robinson River is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.

Robinson River has a limited groundwater source and limited surface water source. Water quality is marginal. The water supply is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Houses and buildings at Robinson River are fitted with private septic systems.

Robinson River is located south east of Borroloola on the banks of the Robinson River and Garawa Aboriginal Land Trust formally the old Robinson River Station.

Name: SANTA TERESA
Description:
The community is located 85km from Alice Springs by road and it takes 1.5 hours to drive there.  By air, it takes 5 minutes to drive to the closest airstrip in the community then 25 minutes to fly to Alice Springs. 

The access road to the community consists of 15 km of sealed road from Alice Springs to the Airport then 68 km of wide, unsealed road, some 10-15 kilometres of which is gravel.  This road is passable for conventional vehicles at most times. A few creek crossings make the road impassable in fairly extreme wet conditions. The road is often quite rough with corrugations and sand and "bulldust" patches are not uncommon.
HistoryDesc:
In 1950, Bishop J P O'Loughlin submitted a grant for land for the Mission. In 1952 Crown land was divided into four blocks with the Catholic Church being granted one of the blocks for a mission which the Church called Santa Teresa.

The Arrernte language name for the community - Ltyentye Apurte - is pronounced " l · jin · jer   port · uh " and means 'clump of beefwood trees'. 

Santa Teresa is named after Carmelite nun Saint Therese of Lisieux who was born in Alencon, France in 1873. Saint Therese of Lisieux was declared a Saint in 1925. Her specific message regarded the missions and that people can be missionaries just by offering help to those less fortunate even though she was restricted to the Carmelite convent. Saint Therese was called the "The Little Flower" in recognition of the message she was spreading throughout the world that little things were more important as big things. 

Santa Teresa is located approx 85km south-east of Alice Springs and 80km from the Simpson Desert. The area for Santa Teresa is a 1,242 square km block of land appropriate for cattle-grazing, located on the Phillipson River normally only a dry creek bed. 

Santa Teresa is positioned at the base of a range of hills overlooking a very large plain. This region of land can be quite vibrant and colourful after the rain when the wild flowers blossom showing off their beautiful colours.

Santa Teresa is administered by the Ltyentye Apurte Community Government Council.

Ltyentye Apurte is the Eastern Arrernte (local Aboriginal group/language) name for a nearby stand of beefwood trees.

The above information is extracted from the council website http://www.ltyentyeapurte.nt.gov.au/home/our_community

Services.Comments: The community is located 85 km from Alice Springs by road and it takes approx 1 hour to drive there.  The access road to the community consists of sealed road (50%) and unsealed gravel road.  The road is passable for conventional vehicles at most times. A few creek crossings make the road impassable in fairly extreme wet conditions.

Projects.Title: TERRITORY WIDE AERODROME FENCING PROGRAM
Projects.Description: THIS PROJECT WILL REPLACE AND UPGRADE THE EXISTING PERIMETER FENCES AND ACCESS GATES AT FIVE AERODROMES SERVICING VERY REMOTE ABORIGINAL COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE TENNANT CREEK AND ALICE SPRINGS REGIONS. THAT IS, CANTEEN CREEK AERODROME, MOUNT LIEBIG AERODROME, ALCOOTA (ENGAWALA) AERODROME, SANTA TERESA AERODROME AND HERMANNSBURG AERODROME. THE UPGRADED HEAVY-DUTY CAMEL FENCES WILL INCREASE THE SAFETY LEVELS FOR INFRASTRUCTURE, AIRCRAFT AND PERSONNEL AS WELL AS RESTRICT ILLEGAL ACCESS TO THE AERODROMES. THIS PROJECT WILL ENHANCE SAFETY AND ACCESS FOR ALL USERS ESPECIALLY FOR DELIVERY OF ESSENTIAL SERVICES INCLUDING AERO-MEDICAL SERVICES.
