HistoryDescription:
In 1950, Bishop J P O'Loughlin submitted a grant for land for the Mission. In 1952 Crown land was divided into four blocks with the Catholic Church being granted one of the blocks for a mission which the Church called Santa Teresa.

The Arrernte language name for the community - Ltyentye Apurte - is pronounced " l · jin · jer   port · uh " and means 'clump of beefwood trees'. 

Santa Teresa is named after Carmelite nun Saint Therese of Lisieux who was born in Alencon, France in 1873. Saint Therese of Lisieux was declared a Saint in 1925. Her specific message regarded the missions and that people can be missionaries just by offering help to those less fortunate even though she was restricted to the Carmelite convent. Saint Therese was called the "The Little Flower" in recognition of the message she was spreading throughout the world that little things were more important as big things. 

Santa Teresa is located approx 85km south-east of Alice Springs and 80km from the Simpson Desert. The area for Santa Teresa is a 1,242 square km block of land appropriate for cattle-grazing, located on the Phillipson River normally only a dry creek bed. 

Santa Teresa is positioned at the base of a range of hills overlooking a very large plain. This region of land can be quite vibrant and colourful after the rain when the wild flowers blossom showing off their beautiful colours.

Santa Teresa is administered by the Ltyentye Apurte Community Government Council.

Ltyentye Apurte is the Eastern Arrernte (local Aboriginal group/language) name for a nearby stand of beefwood trees.

The above information is extracted from the council website http://www.ltyentyeapurte.nt.gov.au/home/our_community

Name: TENNANT CREEK
Description: Tennant Creek is located is located about 1015 kms south of Darwin and 507kms north of Alice Springs. The community can be accessed all year round via the Stuart Highway, the main highway traversing the Northern Territory.
HistoryDesc:
Tennant Creek (stream feature) was named by John McDouall Stuart on 6 June 1860.       

Stuart named the creek after his associate John Tennant of Port Lincon.  The location at which Stuart named the creek is near the Overland Telegraph Station.

Stuart in his journal (SAPP 65 of 1861) wrote:

	"At this place the creek is running E.  Ben, in searching for the horses this morning, found three or four more large waterholes in the creek.  A little SE from this there appears to be an abundance of water in the ranges. ....  This I have named Tennant Creek."

A repeater station was established near Tennant Creek following the completion of the OT Line in 1872.  A reserve was proclaimed around the station in 1874.

Following the discovery of gold in the surrounding hills, the town site of Tennant Creek was surveyed in September 1935.  Blakeway in carrying out the survey took into account the location of the telegraph line and buildings already in existence.

In June 1954 the Town of Tennant Creek was proclaimed.

Projects.Description: THE COMMONWEALTH HEALTH WORKFORCE PROGRAM DELIVERS HEATH WORKFORCE OUTCOMES AND SUPPORT FOR RURAL OUTREACH HEALTH SERVICES. THE HEALTH WORKFORCE PROGRAM IS DELIVERED UNDER THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND AGED CARE&RSQUO;S OUTCOME 1.4 &NDASH; HEALTH WORKFORCE. THIS OUTCOME IS INTENDED TO IMPROVE IMPROVE THE QUALITY, DISTRIBUTION AND PLANNING OF THE AUSTRALIAN HEALTH WORKFORCE TO BETTER MEET THE NEEDS OF THE COMMUNITY AND DELIVER A SUSTAINABLE, WELL DISTRIBUTED HEALTH WORKFORCE. IN THE 2022-23 BUDGET, THE AUSTRALIAN GOVERNMENT ANNOUNCED A LANDMARK LONG-TERM ENGAGEMENT WITH THE ROYAL FLYING DOCTOR SERVICE (RFDS OF AUSTRALIA). THIS ANNOUNCEMENT COMPRISES OF THIS &LSQUO;ENSURING PROVISION OF ESSENTIAL PRIMARY HEALTH CARE SERVICES IN RURAL AND REMOTE AUSTRALIA&RSQUO; PROGRAM, A 10-YEAR STRATEGIC AGREEMENT AND UP TO APPROXIMATELY $1 BILLION OVER A PERIOD OF UP TO TEN YEARS TO PROVIDE ESSENTIAL PRIMARY HEALTH CARE SERVICES AND AEROMEDICAL EVACUATIONS FOR RURAL AND REMOTE PATIENTS IN AREAS OF MARKET FAILURE OR BEYOND WHERE NORMAL MEDICAL INFRASTRUCTURE WOULD OTHERWISE PROVIDE SERVICES. THIS INCLUDES REFORM OF THE COMMONWEALTH&RSQUO;S PARTNERSHIP WITH THE RFDS OF AUSTRALIA TO INCLUDE COLLABORATIVE ANNUAL SERVICE PLANNING, AND INCREASED FLEXIBILITY AND RESPONSIVENESS IN FUNDING ALLOCATION AND SERVICE LEVELS TO ENSURE HEALTH SERVICES ARE DELIVERED TO THOSE COMMUNITIES MOST IN NEED, IN RURAL AND REMOTE AUSTRALIA.&NBSP;&NBSP;

Projects.Title: PACIFICAUS SPORTS GRANTS SUPPORT PARTNERSHIPS IN RUGBY UNION, RUGBY LEAGUE, SOCCER, NETBALL, CRICKET, AFL AND PREPARATIONS FOR THE 2024 PARIS OLYMPICS AND PARALYMPICS, PRIMARILY IN FIJI, NAURU, PAPUA NEW GUINEA, SAMOA, SOLOMON ISLANDS, TONGA AND VANUATU.
Projects.Description: PACIFICAUS SPORTS&RSQUO; PURPOSE IS TO STRENGTHEN PEOPLE-TO-PEOPLE LINKS BETWEEN AUSTRALIA AND THE PACIFIC THROUGH SPORT TO ENHANCE AUSTRALIA&RSQUO;S RELATIONSHIPS AND STANDING IN THE PACIFIC. PACIFICAUS SPORTS DOES THIS BY FOSTERING ELITE SPORT PATHWAYS AND LINKAGES THAT FACILITATE REGULAR COMPETITION AND ENGAGEMENT BETWEEN AUSTRALIA AND PACIFIC TEAMS, ATHLETES AND OTHER SPORT STAKEHOLDERS. THE OBJECTIVES OF PACIFICAUS SPORTS PARTNERSHIP GRANTS ARE: (1) DEVELOPING PATHWAYS FOR PACIFIC TEAMS AND ATHLETES TO PLAY IN HIGH LEVEL AUSTRALIAN SPORTS COMPETITIONS: (2) SUPPORTING AUSTRALIAN SPORTS CODES TO INCREASE THEIR PRESENCE AND PARTICIPATION IN THE PACIFIC; AND (3) DEVELOPING PATHWAYS FOR EMERGING ATHLETES FROM THE REGION TO BENEFIT FROM HIGH PERFORMANCE COACHING, TRAINING, AND COMPETITION. THIS GRANT WILL ENABLE NETBALL AUSTRALIA TO CONTRIBUTE TO THESE OBJECTIVES USING NETBALL THROUGH ACTIVITIES INCLUDING SUPPORT FOR PACIFIC TEAMS AND PLAYERS TO COMPETE AND TRAIN IN AUSTRALIA, SUPPORT FOR AUSTRALIAN NETBALL CLUBS TO ENGAGE WITH THE PACIFIC, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF HIGH PERFORMANCE WORKSHOPS AND COACHING DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS.

Projects.Title: THE AUSTRALIAN CENTRE FOR ADVANCED PHOTOVOLTAICS (ACAP) WAS DESIGNED TO PROVIDE AN INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR A COORDINATED, NATIONAL APPROACH TO SOLAR PV RESEARCH IN AUSTRALIA. IT AIMS TO DEVELOP OVER THE HORIZON PV TECHNOLOGY TO CREATE A PIPELINE OF
Projects.Description:
DELIVERED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF NEW SOUTH WALES (UNSW) SCHOOL OF PHOTOVOLTAIC AND RENEWABLE ENERGY ENGINEERING, ACAP INCLUDES RESEARCH GROUPS AT CSIRO, AUSTRALIAN NATIONAL UNIVERSITY, UNIVERSITY OF MELBOURNE, UNIVERSITY OF QUEENSLAND, UNIVERSITY OF SYDNEY AND MONASH UNIVERSITY. THE PROJECT PROVIDES A PIPELINE TO &LSQUO;OVER THE HORIZON&RSQUO; PHOTOVOLTAIC TECHNOLOGY, AS WELL AS TRAINING THE NEXT GENERATION OF RESEARCH SCIENTISTS AND ENGINEERS THROUGH EXPOSURE TO WORLD-CLASS FACILITIES ACROSS AUSTRALIA AND THE WORLD AND ESTABLISHING AUSTRALIA AS THE PHOTOVOLTAIC RESEARCH AND EDUCATIONAL HUB OF THE ASIA-PACIFIC REGION.
THE ACAP PROJECT COMMENCED IN DECEMBER 2012 AND PREVIOUSLY RECEIVED GRANT FUNDING OF $83.99M, TAKING THE TOTAL AMOUNT OF GRANT FUNDING TO DATE TO $128.99M.

HistoryDescription:
Tennant Creek (stream feature) was named by John McDouall Stuart on 6 June 1860.       

Stuart named the creek after his associate John Tennant of Port Lincon.  The location at which Stuart named the creek is near the Overland Telegraph Station.

Stuart in his journal (SAPP 65 of 1861) wrote:

	"At this place the creek is running E.  Ben, in searching for the horses this morning, found three or four more large waterholes in the creek.  A little SE from this there appears to be an abundance of water in the ranges. ....  This I have named Tennant Creek."

A repeater station was established near Tennant Creek following the completion of the OT Line in 1872.  A reserve was proclaimed around the station in 1874.

Following the discovery of gold in the surrounding hills, the town site of Tennant Creek was surveyed in September 1935.  Blakeway in carrying out the survey took into account the location of the telegraph line and buildings already in existence.

In June 1954 the Town of Tennant Creek was proclaimed.

	(2)	Wilson, Helen - The Heritage of Tennant Creek.

Name: TI TREE
Description: The Town is located 180km north of Alice Springs.
HistoryDesc:
A well on the banks of the Woodforde Creek was named "Tea Tree Well" during the construction of the Overland Telagraph Line (refer A T Woods O T Line construction records) and is believed to be named as the well was amongst "tea tree" bushes in the creek.

In the 1920's with pastoral expansion north of Alice Springs, William Heffernan founded Ti Tree Station, some miles west of the well, and eventually a store was set up by Lily Hese at Tea Tree Well.

In early 1980 the community requested, by petition to Legislative Assembly, that the spelling of the town name be changed from "Tea Tree" to "Ti-Tree".  The area of the town was gazetted on 15 May 1981 with the town being officially named "Ti-Tree" on 22 April 1983 (NTG18 6 May 1983).

In 1994 the Town of Ti-Tree was incorporated into the Anmatjere Community Government Council.

HistoryDescription:
A well on the banks of the Woodforde Creek was named "Tea Tree Well" during the construction of the Overland Telagraph Line (refer A T Woods O T Line construction records) and is believed to be named as the well was amongst "tea tree" bushes in the creek.

In the 1920's with pastoral expansion north of Alice Springs, William Heffernan founded Ti Tree Station, some miles west of the well, and eventually a store was set up by Lily Hese at Tea Tree Well.

In early 1980 the community requested, by petition to Legislative Assembly, that the spelling of the town name be changed from "Tea Tree" to "Ti-Tree".  The area of the town was gazetted on 15 May 1981 with the town being officially named "Ti-Tree" on 22 April 1983 (NTG18 6 May 1983).

In 1994 the Town of Ti-Tree was incorporated into the Anmatjere Community Government Council.

Name: TIMBER CREEK
Description: The Town is located 265km SW from Katherine. This double lane sealed road is well maintained. National Coach lines pass through each day (both ways). Timber Creek is nestled in the Victoria River valley escarpment country. Timber Creek lies at the central point on the Victoria Highway between Katherine and Kununurra. The trip from Katherine to Timber Creek takes about three hours.
HistoryDesc:
The town of Timber Creek takes its name from the stream of the same name which A C Gregory, of the North Australian Expedition, named on 24 November 1855 when examining the Victoria River and seeking timber to repair his boat Tom Tough.  He was later to explore the Victoria River District.  
A police station (Burmaioni) was established on the banks of the Victoria River in the vicinity of Timber Creek in the mid 1890s and in 1911 Phillip Hutchison established a depot to service the outlying pastoral stations.
In post-war years when the Victoria Highway was improved, attempts were made to design a small townsite in the area.  A townsite was proclaimed on 20 June 1975 (NTG 24).  The Timber Creek Community Government Council has controlled this area of 16 square kilometres since 6 November 1992.

Services.Comments: Timber Creek is located approx 265 km along the Victoria Highway. This double lane sealed road is well maintained. It is one of two public access points to the Victoria River, the other being the VR Roadhouse 92 km east. The trip from Katherine to Timber Creek takes about three hours .

AliasNameDescription: The community Timber Creek is not known to have any other aliases.
HistoryDescription:
The town of Timber Creek takes its name from the stream of the same name which A C Gregory, of the North Australian Expedition, named on 24 November 1855 when examining the Victoria River and seeking timber to repair his boat Tom Tough.  He was later to explore the Victoria River District.  
A police station (Burmaioni) was established on the banks of the Victoria River in the vicinity of Timber Creek in the mid 1890s and in 1911 Phillip Hutchison established a depot to service the outlying pastoral stations.
In post-war years when the Victoria Highway was improved, attempts were made to design a small townsite in the area.  A townsite was proclaimed on 20 June 1975 (NTG 24).  The Timber Creek Community Government Council has controlled this area of 16 square kilometres since 6 November 1992.

Name: TITJIKALA
Description: The community is located 130 km south of Alice Springs via the Old South Road -4WD track. It takes 1.5 hours to drive there. The road from Alice Springs is unsealed. The main access to the community is by the old south road, which parallels the Old Ghan train line running south from Alice Springs (approximately 130 km). The old south road is formed and partly gravelled. Access is generally available to conventional vehicles, however the road becomes impassable after heavy rains. The Department of Transport and Works undertake routine maintenance of the road.

Titjikala has a fully reticulated sewerage system.

Name: UMBAKUMBA
Description:
The community is located approximately 50 km east of Angurugu situated inside Little Lagoon, Point Langton on the northeast coast of Groote Eylandt.  Umbakumba is approximately 50 km east of Angurugu on Groote Eylandt, which is 650 km east of Darwin and 50 km off the Arnhem Land coast in the Gulf of Carpentaria.  

Apart from the fortnightly freight barge service from Darwin, Umbakumba is generally accessed by air.  Groote Eylandt airport, located 1 km from Angurugu, is the main air access point for the island.  Owned and maintained by Gemco, the airstrip is sealed and there are flights to and from Nhulunbuy/Darwin most days.  Travel time to Nhulunbuy: 30-50 minutes, to Darwin: 1.5-2 hours.  A 50 km dirt road links Angurugu to Umbakumba.

Charter flights can also be arranged direct to Umbakumba which has a dirt airstrip that can accommodate twin engine light aircraft.  There is a reasonable dirt road from the airport to Umbakumba.  However, a 4-wheel drive is essential and given the number of rivers and streams, travel throughout the island during the wet season can be difficult.

Services.Comments:
There is no regular transport to Umbakumba community but flights are available at the major Groote Eylandt airport which is at Angurugu (approximately 50 kilometres away).


Umbakumba has an unsealed airstrip that can be utilised during the dry season.

The community is 270km south-west of Darwin in the Daly River Reserve at the mouth of the Fitzmaurice River, close to the coast of the Joseph Bonaparte Gulf. 
By road it is 417kms from Darwin. By air it is slightly over 1 Hrs flying time from Darwin (Twin Engine)(270km)

Wadeye has very good quality fluoridated water with an adequate groundwater supply.
Wadeye has a fully reticulated sewerage system.

Name: WALLACE ROCKHOLE
Description:
The community is located 120 km west from Alice Springs and 20 km south of Hermannsburg road. It takes 1? hours to drive there. By air, it takes 20 minutes to drive to the closest airstrip in Ntaria and 35 minutes to fly to Alice Springs.

The access road to the community consists of 100km of sealed road from Alice Springs and then 20 km of graded dirt road. This road is passable for conventional vehicles at most times though it is rough in the wet. In extreme weather the road is impassable and the town can become isolated.

NewsEvents.Title: Wallace Rockhole - Local Authority Meeting

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Wallace Rockhole is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply. Wallace Rockhole is connected to the Alice Springs electricity grid.
Wallace Rockhole has a plentiful groundwater source with adequate water quality, disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Houses and buildings at Wallace Rockhole are fitted with private septic systems.
Western Arrernte
MacDonnell Regional Council
Namatjira
Wallace Rockhole is located west of Alice Springs on the Uruna Aboriginal Land Trust and is near Henbury and Owen Springs Pastoral Properties.

Name: WUGULARR
Description: The community is located on the banks of Waterhouse River approximately 118 km south east of Katherine and 31 km east of Barunga. By road, it takes approximately 1.5 hours to travel from Katherine.
HistoryDesc:
Formerly known as Beswick, in 2024 the community name was changed at the request of the Bagala Traditional Owners. 

Wugularr is the Jawoyn language place name that refers to the Country where the community sits today. 

The previous name Beswick was adopted from the former pastoral lease known as Beswick Station, the station name being derived from the nearby stream Beswick Creek.

Services.Comments: By road, the community is located approximately 118 km south east of Katherine and 31 km east of Barunga. It's around 1.5 hours' drive from Katherine. The Central Arnhem Highway is sealed to the Wugularr Rubbish Dump, approximately 6km past Wugularr. Only during severe flooding which occurs only sporadically does the road become inaccessible.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Wugularr is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply. Wugularr is connected to the Katherine electricity grid.
Wugularr has a plentiful groundwater source with marginal quality water, which is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Wugularr has a fully reticulated sewerage system.
Eastside Kriol
Roper Gulf Regional Council
Stuart
Wugularr is located on the banks of the Waterhouse River east of Katherine on the Beswick Aboriginal Land Trust.

HistoryDescription:
Formerly known as Beswick, in 2024 the community name was changed at the request of the Bagala Traditional Owners. 

Wugularr is the Jawoyn language place name that refers to the Country where the community sits today. 

The previous name Beswick was adopted from the former pastoral lease known as Beswick Station, the station name being derived from the nearby stream Beswick Creek.

Name: WURRUMIYANGA
Description: The community is located on the south-east corner of Bathurst Island, which is part of the Tiwi Islands. It is approximately 70km NNW of Darwin or 20 minutes by air.
HistoryDesc:
Originally established as a Mission by the Catholic Church on Bathurst Island at the southern entrance to Apsley Strait.

During the World War II defence of Darwin the Mission had the code name ARSY.

In the 1980s the name of this Community changed to Nguiu.

In 2010, the Community name was altered from Nguiu to Wurrumiyanga, as requested by the Tiwi Land Council, on advice from Traditional Land Owners.

Wurrumiyanga is the local Tiwi name for the area where the community is built, meaning "the place where the cycads grow".

HistoryDescription:
Originally established as a Mission by the Catholic Church on Bathurst Island at the southern entrance to Apsley Strait.

During the World War II defence of Darwin the Mission had the code name ARSY.

In the 1980s the name of this Community changed to Nguiu.

In 2010, the Community name was altered from Nguiu to Wurrumiyanga, as requested by the Tiwi Land Council, on advice from Traditional Land Owners.

Wurrumiyanga is the local Tiwi name for the area where the community is built, meaning "the place where the cycads grow".

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Wutunugurra  is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Wutunugurra has a limited groundwater source with very good quality water, which is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Houses and buildings at Wutunugurra are fitted with private septic systems.
Alyawarr
Barkly Regional Council
Barkly
Wutunugurra is located south east of Tennant Creek, on the western side of the Frew River on a Community Living Area within the Epenarra Pastoral Property.

Name: YARRALIN
Description: The community is situated on the banks of the Wickham River close to the Victoria River, 380 km southwest of Katherine. Main access is from the sealed Victoria Highway and then through the picturesque Jasper Gorge (unsealed) which is often impassable during the wet season. Alternative access is from the Buntine Highway through Top Springs. A one-way trip from Katherine to the community will take approximately 4 ? hours. Apart from the Victoria Highway all roads are unsealed gravel and often rocky.

Services.Comments: Access from Katherine is via the Victoria Highway and then through the picturesque Jasper Gorge, often impassable during the wet season. Alternative access is via the Buntine Highway through Top Springs. Apart from the Victoria Highway all roads are unsealed and often rocky. It takes around 4 hours to drive there from Katherine.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Yarralin is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Yarralin has a limited groundwater source with marginal quality water, which is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Yarralin has a fully reticulated sewerage system.
Ngarinyman / Kriol
Victoria Daly Regional Council
Stuart
Yarralin is located on the banks of the Wickham River south west of Katherine on the Ngalkarrang-Wulngann Aboriginal Land Trust surrounded by the Victoria River Downs Pastoral Property.

Name: YIRRKALA
Description: The community of Yirrkala is located south east of Nhulunbuy CBD on Cape Arnhem.  Yirrkala is 18 km south east of Nhulunbuy CBD.  From Nhulunbuy CBD the community is accessible via the Central Arnhem Road.  Travel time is approximately 15 mins.

Services.Comments: Yirrkala is 15 km southeast of Nhulunbuy by road. From Nhulunbuy CBD the community is accessible via the Central Arnhem Road. Travel time is approximately 15 mins.
Check Road Report NT and Check the tides before travelling
Gove Peninsula Public Bus (NEAL) runs between Yirrkala - Gumatj Retail Precinct - Gunyangara, Monday - Saturday, and costs $10/person. General enquiries 8987 0900.
Available at Rirratjingu Fuel by Yirrkala Oval and BP in Nhulunbuy (15km north of Yirrkala).
General Restricted Area. Alcohol restrictions in effect.
Active Volatile Substance Management Plan in community.

Yirrkala Guest House , operated by Buku Larnggary Mulka 8987 1701

Commercial Accommodation available in Nhulunbuy approximately 19 km north-west of the community. These include Yanawal Units, Walkabout Lodge and Campsite, Manyimi Campground, BanuBanu Lodge and Wallaby Beach Accommodation (also known as the Rirratjingu Workers Camp) another 4km north towards Gunyangara.
Yirrkala Community Store (08 8987 2324) sells groceries, fresh produce and hot food. Opening hours are Monday to Friday 8am - 6pm, and Saturday 9am - 2pm.
Nhulunbuy Airport is situated 10km west of Yirrkala, approximately a 10 min drive.

Primary Health Care delivered by Miwatja Health Aboriginal Corporation (08) 8987 2650

Opening Hours:

Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday: 8:30am - 4pm

Wednesday: 1pm - 4pm
Serviced from Nhulunbuy Police Station (est distance 20 km) (8987 1333)

Yirrkala Bilingual School is operated by the Department of Education (8987 1988), and provides a FaFT program (0 to 5yrs), and Preschool to Year 12.

The Laynhapuy Homelands School office is also located in Yirrkala.

Both are Limited program schools for ABSTUDY and Youth Allowance, for more information.
East Arnhem Regional Council - Yirrkala Office (08) 8939 2409 operates Monday to Friday 8am to 4:30pm.

Laynhapuy Homelands Aboriginal Corporation delivers the Remote Australia Employment Services (RAES) program which replaced the former CDP program across the Gove Peninsula and surrounding East Arnhem Land homelands.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Yirrkala is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Yirrkala has a plentiful groundwater source with very good quality water, disinfected with sodium hypochlorite and monitored monthly for microbes.
Yirrkala has a fully reticulated sewerage system.

Name: YUELAMU
Description:
The community is located 290 km northwest of Alice Springs on the old Mt Allen Pastoral lease. By road it takes 3 ? hours to drive there. When flying, it takes 5 minutes to drive to the closest airstrip in the community then 40 minutes to fly to Alice Springs.

The road from Alice Springs to the community is both sealed & unsealed. The access road to the community is via the Tanami Highway off the Stuart Highway. The first 145 km from the Stuart Highway is sealed with the next 117 km being dirt. The turnoff to the community is approximately 65 km past Tilmouth Wells. From there it is 31 km on unformed gravel road to the community.

From the Tanami Highway the road is in fair condition but is subject to washaways during heavy rainfall, particularly where it crosses the natural depressions and minor waterways.

Services.Comments: The access road to the community from Alice Springs is via the Tanami Highway off the Stuart Highway. The road from the Stuart Highway to the Mt Allen turnoff is sealed.  From there it is 31 km unformed gravel road to the community. From the Tanami Highway the road is subject to washaways during heavy rainfall.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Yuelamu is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply. Yuelamu is connected to the Yuendumu electricity grid.

Yuelamu is currently provided with treated drinking water collected by residents from an advanced water treatment plant that is connected to a non-potable bore. Non-potable water for hygiene only usage is supplied to residents through the existing water reticulation system. A dual reticulation system to supply both potable and non-potable water to households is currently under construction. The surface water dam which previously supplied the community with potable water is unusable due to long term contamination from blue green algae.
Yuelamu has a fully reticulated sewerage system.
Anmatyerr / Warlpiri
Central Desert Regional Council
Stuart
Yuelamu is located north west of Alice Springs on the Yalpirakinu Aboriginal Land Trust south of Mount Denison Pastoral Property.

Name: YUENDUMU
Description:
The community is located 290km North West from Alice Springs along the Tanami Highway, which branches off the Stuart Highway 25 km North of Alice Springs. It takes 3 1/2 hours to drive there. The road is sealed for the first 145 km from the highway and the rest of the way is formed and largely gravelled with some sections not gravelled. The road can be quite corrugated but is usually passable for ordinary vehicles except after heavy rains.

The access to the community after the turn off from the Tanami Road is 3 km, of which the first 1 km is gravelled and the balance is sealed and 6.2 m wide.

ProfileSections.Content: Electricity at Yuendumu is supplied to all customers at the Northern Territory standard tariff and standard connection charges apply.
Yuendumu has a good quality water supply drawn from very limited groundwater sources. Community demand is continuously monitored to ensure that adequate supply can be maintained.
Yuendumu has a fully reticulated sewerage system.
Warlpiri
Central Desert Regional Council
Stuart

Yuendumu is located on the edge of the Tanami Desert north west of Alice Springs on the Yuendumu Aboriginal Land Trust. The Land Trust boarders Mount Doreen, Mount Denison, Central Mount Wedge and Mount Allan Pastoral Properties.

Name: YULARA
Description: The Town is located 340km WSW of Alice Springs.
HistoryDesc:
Following the Northern Territory Administration decision to establish a new town near Ayers Rock in 1975 to service the tourist industry associated with Ayers Rock and The Olgas, the Place Names Committee in consultation with the Ayers Rock Advisory Committee and local aboriginals recommended the new town site be called YULARA (NTG 49 of 12/12/1975)  - after the aboriginal word for "howling dingo" and the associated "Dingo dreaming".

The Town of Yulara boundaries were gazetted in 1976 (NTG 34 of 20/8/1976 ).

The NT Government transferred the majority of the land, roads and buildings within the Town boundary to  Ayers Rock Resort Nominees Pty Ltd in August 1992  (NTG 34 of 26/8/1992).

THE ACAP PROJECT COMMENCED IN DECEMBER 2012 AND PREVIOUSLY RECEIVED GRANT FUNDING OF $83.99M, TAKING THE TOTAL AMOUNT OF GRANT FUNDING TO DATE TO $128.99M.

HistoryDescription:
Following the Northern Territory Administration decision to establish a new town near Ayers Rock in 1975 to service the tourist industry associated with Ayers Rock and The Olgas, the Place Names Committee in consultation with the Ayers Rock Advisory Committee and local aboriginals recommended the new town site be called YULARA (NTG 49 of 12/12/1975)  - after the aboriginal word for "howling dingo" and the associated "Dingo dreaming".

The Town of Yulara boundaries were gazetted in 1976 (NTG 34 of 20/8/1976 ).

The NT Government transferred the majority of the land, roads and buildings within the Town boundary to  Ayers Rock Resort Nominees Pty Ltd in August 1992  (NTG 34 of 26/8/1992).
